```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(factoextra)


lithics_clean <- read_csv("lithics_clean.csv")


```


```{r}
# prepare the data for PCA
pca_data <-
  lithics_clean |> 
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  drop_na()

# compute PCA
pca_result <-
  prcomp(pca_data, scale. = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# k-means clustering ------------------------------------------------------
# cluster on the standardised variables (not on the PCA scores) so that the
# full variation in the data is used, not just the first two dimensions
set.seed(459)

km_data <- scale(pca_data)

# how many clusters? elbow (within-cluster sum of squares) + silhouette
avg_silhouette <- function(k) {
  km <- kmeans(km_data, centers = k, nstart = 25)
  mean(cluster::silhouette(km$cluster, dist(km_data))[, "sil_width"])
}

km_diagnostics <-
  tibble(
    k          = 2:8,
    withinss   = map_dbl(2:8, ~ kmeans(km_data, centers = .x, nstart = 25)$tot.withinss),
    silhouette = map_dbl(2:8, avg_silhouette)
  )
km_diagnostics

# k = 3 is the elbow of the withinss curve and gives the smallest set of
# cleanly separated groups (they also track the three artefact periods)
k <- 3
km_result <- kmeans(km_data, centers = k, nstart = 25)

# cluster membership, in the same row order as pca_data and pca_result$x
km_cluster <- factor(km_result$cluster,
                     levels  = 1:k,
                     labels = paste("Cluster", 1:k))

km_membership <-
  lithics_clean |>
  slice(as.integer(rownames(pca_data))) |>
  mutate(cluster = km_cluster)

km_membership |> count(cluster)

# how the clusters line up with the archaeological periods
table(km_membership$period, km_membership$cluster)
```

```{r}
#1 label: fig-pca-biplot
#1 fig-cap: This biplot shows the different types and the variables used to classify them. For example, the blue would have the largest weight, width, thickness, etc, and the green would have the shortest length and moderate thickness. 

fviz_pca(pca_result,
         geom.ind = "point",
         col.ind = km_cluster,
         shape.ind = 19,
         addEllipses = TRUE,
         repel = TRUE,
         title = "") +
  labs(colour = "Cluster") +
  guides(fill = "none")

        
```

```{r}
# label: fig-pca-contr 
#1 fig-cap: This figure shows the dimensions and their eigen value. Only the first 4 are above the eigen value of one and dimension one is much more significant since it is high above the line. 

# how much each PC is telling us
fviz_eig(pca_result,
         choice = "eigenvalue",
         parallel = TRUE, 
         title = "")
```

```{r}
# label: fig-pca-contri-original 
# fig-cap: This figure shows which variables contribute the most to dimension 1. This shows that width, weight, thickness, and platform all play an important role, while elongation, length, and giur aren't as important to classification of clusters. This is evident in the biplot, as you can see cluster three has the largest width, weight, and platform, with cluster two having the second largest and cluster 3 third largest. Cluster 2 has the shortest length, but cluster 1 and 3 are similar in length. Largest elongation belongs to cluster 1, and cluster 2 and 3 are similar.

fviz_contrib(pca_result, 
             choice = "var", 
             axes = 1)
```
